children: faces closer scrutiny over its earnings quality, with shares at $373.64, down approximately 0.25%, around 10.55 a.m. ET Friday. According to Barron's, roughly $786 million in tariff refunds supported margins. That puts a sharper question in front of investors: how much of the improvement can Tesla deliver again?

Tesla's quarterly update showed revenue of $28.05 billion, essentially flat from a year earlier, while operating income fell 56% to $718 million. Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits reached 18.1%. Cash generation offered a brighter spot: operating cash flow of $6.26 billion covered $4.73 billion in capital spending, leaving $1.53 billion in free cash flow. Still, steady sales alongside sharply lower operating profit leave plenty to prove.

The valuation graphic puts Tesla 6.44% above its $351.03 GF Value estimate, suggesting the shares already carry a premium despite the earnings pressure. Refunds can help one quarter; sustained profitability needs repeatable gains in pricing, manufacturing efficiency and subscription revenue. Investors should watch whether those gains can support margins as robotaxi, robotics and semiconductor investments compete for cash.

title: Tesla Stocks Edge Lower as Refunds Blur the Margin Beat
